title: LatticeWave: latency vs cost (text charts) - brief
content:
Executive summary:

This brief records a compact set of microbenchmarks run against two serving configurations for an interactive chat workload with short turns (median 24 tokens), designed to highlight microburst behavior and the cost/latency frontier. The goal: produce readable text charts that can be dropped into a one-pager or used as collateral while we iterate on visual dashboards.

Key takeaways:
- Hybrid-prefetch (FP16 dynamic-batching + lightweight prefetch) gives the best median (p50) latency at modest cost, but degrades on p99 during microbursts.
- Compact-quant (8-bit Q4-like) yields ~18-22% lower $/M tokens for sustained throughput but shows a consistent +8–12 ms p50 penalty on short-turn interactions.
- KV-cache hitrate >60% is a decisive lever: at 60–80% hitrange the compact-quant config approaches parity on p90 with hybrid-prefetch while keeping cost savings.

Bench overview:
- Workload: synthetic chat-turn replay derived from product telemetry (sampled 10k sessions, median turn 24 tokens, 95th percentile session length 9 turns). We created a microburst profile: 30 concurrent sessions generating a 5s spike window every 120s.
- Models tested: open-llm-13b (baseline FP16), open-llm-13b-quant (8-bit compact profile), open-llm-13b-hybrid (FP16 + decode-prefetch heuristics).
- Hardware: gpubox-g5x (A100-like 80GB) and gpubox-h100-sim (H100-like). All tests run on dedicated single-GPU instances to isolate per-GPU scheduling effects.
- Harness: stateless HTTP client with controlled think-time, 3 warmup minutes, 15 minute measurement window, token-level cost capture.

Measured metrics (definitions):
- p50, p90, p99: end-to-end server-side latency from request accepted to final token emit.
- cost_per_m_tokens: dollars per million output tokens (includes GPU amortized runtime + model license tier).
- kv_hitrate: fraction of requests served with valid cached KV prefix (where applicable).

Condensed numeric table (median of runs):

Config | hw | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p99(ms) | $/M tokens | kv_hitrate
-------|----|---------|---------|---------|------------|---------
Hybrid-prefetch | gpubox-g5x | 34 | 78 | 210 | 48.2 | 21%
Compact-quant | gpubox-g5x | 42 | 86 | 180 | 38.7 | 22%
Hybrid-prefetch | gpubox-h100-sim | 28 | 64 | 160 | 45.0 | 19%
Compact-quant | gpubox-h100-sim | 36 | 72 | 140 | 33.2 | 20%

Interpretation notes:
- On g5x hardware the compact-quant option reduces $/M by ~20% relative to hybrid-prefetch but increases median latency by ~8ms. p99 is actually better for compact-quant in these runs because quantization reduces decode CPU-side jitter; we observed fewer long tail stalls tied to kernel switching.
- On H100-like hardware compact-quant is both cheaper and closer in latency (hardware favors the quant kernel optimizations).
- KV-cache hitrate in these synthetic runs is low (~20%) because the synthetic workload shuffles prefixes to exercise cold-path. Real product traffic with higher prefix reuse will shift the frontier toward compact-quant.

ASCII tradeoff curve (cost vs p90) — each line is a config point, numbers are (p90 ms, $/M)

        |                          . (Hybrid g5x 78,48.2)
  p90   |           . (Hybrid h100 64,45.0)
   ms   |      . (Compact g5x 86,38.7)
        |   . (Compact h100 72,33.2)
        +----------------------------------------
            lower cost <-------------------------> higher cost

Microburst timeline (text histogram, p99 over time sample):
Time(s) | p99(ms)
0–30    | 160
30–60   | 205   <- spike window observed higher p99 for hybrid-prefetch
60–90   | 142
90–120  | 155
120–150 | 210   <- repeated microburst
150–180 | 148

Observations from timing traces:
- Hybrid-prefetch shows spiky p99 aligned to admission windows where dynamic batching aggregated short-turn requests into larger decode windows; batching helps throughput but increases worst-case latency when bursts align.
- Compact-quant kept smaller jitter because the compute path stayed within a narrow kernel set, avoiding occasional kernel rebinds we observed in hybrid mode.

Sensitivity sweep: kv_hitrate vs p90 (compact-quant, gpubox-h100-sim)
kv_hitrate | p90(ms) | $/M
-----------|---------|-----
10%        | 78      | 36.8
30%        | 66      | 34.0
50%        | 56      | 31.0
70%        | 48      | 29.1

Takeaway: hitting >50% KV cache effectively buys ~20ms p90 improvement for compact-quant with incremental cost reductions.

Recommendations (short):
- For customer tiers that prioritize median latency (interactive low-latency UX) choose hybrid-prefetch on g5x; for customers focused on unit economics (large sustained embedding/chat throughput) offer compact-quant on H100-like hardware or with explicit prefill/kvcaching incentives.
- Instrument product telemetry to report session-level prefix reuse (a small feature flag) to estimate expected kv_hitrate; we can provide a quick ROI calc to customers.
- Add a dashboard band showing cost/lateness frontier (p90 vs $/M) as a quick compare widget in Console. Use text table export like this doc for emailable collateral.

Open questions / next experiments:
- Re-run with real request ordering (not synthetic shuffles) to validate KV hitrate distribution.
- Try a 12-minute longer-run to see whether packing improvements emerge at T>20 minutes (we saw small drift in throughput).
- Evaluate mixed-tenant scenarios (two model sizes sharing slab) — do quant kernels preserve tail-stability under multi-tenant coil?

Appendix: quick reproducibility notes
- harness: bench-client v0.9.2 (internal) with --microburst-profile cycle=120s spike=5s concurrency=30 seed=42
- models: open-llm-13b@fp16, open-llm-13b@q4-8bit, open-llm-13b@hybrid-prefetch (branch hybrid-decode v3)
- git refs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime (see PR #78 for kernel-tuning patch)
- raw csvs stored in: s3://redwood-bench/latticewave/2026-04-18/ (internal access)

Notes to self:
- Convert these ascii charts into small svg sparklines for the next share.
- Ask Priya to add kv_hitrate as a dimension in the p90 cohort dashboard.

End of brief.
